thought.text: The backend fails to load an ESM dependency under Node 20. The deployment runs Node 22 (which supports `require(esm)`). Let me use Node 22.

reasoning_content:
The production build uses the same ESM issue likely. Let me try the production build to see if it bundles differently. Actually the issue is webpack leaving @trpc-limiter/memory as external require. In production config, `generatePackageJson: true` and webpack may externalize node_modules differently... Actually the dev build also used generatePackageJson. Let me check the production build for backend, maybe the output is same.

Let me look at how Nx webpack handles externals. Actually, the simplest workaround for running: the guide says to run `npm run back` which uses `nx serve` (build + node). That would hit the same issue.

Wait, maybe production build works. Let me build production backend.

Actually the issue: webpack config `target: "node"` with nx - by default nx externalizes all deps for node target. Then `require("@trpc-limiter/memory")` is used which is ESM. In production, they run with node:22 which... Node 22 supports require(esm) by default! Node 20.18 also has `--experimental-require-module`. Actually Node 22.12+ supports require(ESM) unflagged. The compose uses node:22.18.0. So production works on node 22.

We installed node 20.18. Let me just run with node 22. Or run with flag `--experimental-require-module`.

Let me check if node 20.18 supports the flag.
